open_questions: Why are transit depths so scattered (QLP vs SPOC and sector-to-sector)? Is it astrophysical depth change or low-SNR false alarm with spot contamination?
Does the odd/even modulation persist with higher precision? Resolution to 6.6 d would rule out binary at twice period.
dossier.public_summary: This is a 3 Earth-radius dip every 13.2 days on a small M dwarf with a flat bottom and no secondary eclipse. Depths vary a lot from transit to transit and between TESS data sources, and odd vs even dips differ at low significance. The data are low signal-to-noise (SNR ~10) and show no clear off-target source. Better and more uniform photometry and a test of the 13.2-day vs 6.6-day period are needed to decide if this is a planet or a false alarm.

reasons.why: Depth looks to change between sectors; SPOC gives 4968 ppm and 6377 ppm, QLP gives 725 ppm and 4542 ppm.
Change is between light-curve products (calibration) not apparent within SPOC (p_constant 0.2799838330073936), as expected for low-SNR light vs contamination/systematics.
Individual transits show very large scatter, much larger than formal errors, and a few carry almost all signal.
Odd/even depths differ at low significance but consistently in 2 sectors (sector_oe_max_sigma 4.211, sector_oe_sectors_over_3 2), also reported by xgboost planet_rank 0.11.
No difference image to rule out a neighbour; neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0 and could_cause_within_1px 0 keep neighbour unlikely but inconclusive.
